subject: Post-demo summary & proposed geo + competitive tests
messages:
From: Jasmine Liu <jasmine@redwood.com>
To: David Park <david.park@healthtech.ai>
Cc: Emily Chen <emily.chen@healthtech.ai>
Date: Mon, 19 Oct 2026 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Post-demo summary & proposed geo + competitive tests

Hi David / Emily,

Thanks again for the demo time today — appreciated the context on your real-time summarization use case and the per-region regulatory constraints. Below is a short recap + proposed next tests so we can come back with a quantified comparison vs the hyperscalers you mentioned.

Recap (what we heard)
- Primary workload: real-time clinical note summarization (short prompts, high QPS spikes)
- Data residency: EU patient records must not leave eu-west for any processing steps
- Success metrics: median token latency under 120ms in target regions; sustained 250 qps at P95 for peak windows

Proposed next tests (suggested, can refine)
1) Geo latency sweep (three regions): us-west1, eu-west1, ap-south1 — 50k requests each with representative prompt set
2) Throughput ramp: sustained throughput profile to identify when tail latency increases (250, 500, 1k qps buckets)
3) Residency & access test: confirm routing and private deployment constraints for eu-west only data (end-to-end flow)
4) Competitive head-to-head: run the same prompts against Redwood hosted endpoints and a small set of hyperscaler endpoints (Bedrock / Vertex AI / Azure OA) for latency and cost-per-token comparison

Attachments: redwood-vs-hyperscaler-onepager.pdf (PDF, 92KB), demo-recording-20261019.mp4 (video, 18MB)

Can you confirm the following so we can schedule the tech sync with Sergio (our SE) and produce the test harness?
- A representative prompt set (or permission to use a synthetic seed)
- Any IP/PII redaction we should apply for test runs
- Target week for the tests (we can run them as early as next week)

If that sounds good I’ll loop in Sergio and send a brief test plan + calendar invites.

Best,
Jasmine Liu
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
jasmine@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0134

--

From: Jasmine Liu <jasmine@redwood.com>
To: David Park <david.park@healthtech.ai>
Cc: Emily Chen <emily.chen@healthtech.ai>, Sergio Alvarez <sergio@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 20 Oct 2026 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-demo summary & proposed geo + competitive tests

David — great, thanks for the quick clarifications. Short answers inline and next steps below.

- Ballpark cost: for the workload you described we typically see ~30–40% lower per-token unit costs on Redwood hosted vs single-region hyperscaler managed endpoints due to batching and prefix caching; Dedicated pools (reserved capacity) give another ~15–25% improvement but require a monthly commit. I attached a quick CSV with preliminary estimates by model tier (prelim-cost-estimates.csv). These are indicative — we’ll refine once we see your actual prompt mix.

- Competitive endpoints: for an apples-to-apples test we can run the hyperscaler endpoints from our side when customers provide short-term test keys (preferred) OR we can provide a harness and instructions if you want to run the comparisons inside your environment. Either works — running from our side helps control for network variance but you may prefer running from your VPC for strict residency testing.

Next steps I propose:
1) I’ll schedule a 30-min tech sync with Sergio (SE) to finalize the prompt set and residency constraints — available slots Tue/Wed 2–5pm PT
2) You drop the redacted prompt files to the Drive link and flag which prompts are EU-only
3) We’ll run a 3-region latency sweep and produce a short comparison table (latency distribution + cost per 1k tokens)

Looping in Sergio to confirm the technical plan and test matrix. Sergio — can you confirm the probe specs and whether we need any infra access from HealthTech for accurate measurements?

Thanks,
Jasmine

Attachment: prelim-cost-estimates.csv (CSV, 5KB)
From: Sergio Alvarez <sergio@redwood.com>
To: Jasmine Liu <jasmine@redwood.com>, David Park <david.park@healthtech.ai>
Cc: Emily Chen <emily.chen@healthtech.ai>
Date: Tue, 20 Oct 2026 09:42:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-demo summary & proposed geo + competitive tests

Hi all — quick technical note and draft test plan. High level: we can run the head-to-heads from Redwood-hosted runners or provide a lightweight harness you can execute in your environment. For residency-sensitive tests we’ll need the runs executed inside eu-west1 (either our private deployment or your VPC).

Draft test matrix (short):
- Regions: us-west1 (Oregon), us-east4 (N. Virginia), eu-west1 (Frankfurt), ap-south1 (Mumbai) — will sample at least 50k requests per region
- Payloads: 3 buckets (short prompts 20–40 tokens, medium 80–150 tokens, long 300+ tokens)
- Probes: single-request latency, 95/99p tail, and sustained QPS ramps at 250/500/1000
- Comparison targets: Redwood-hosted (recommended), Redwood Dedicated (if committed), AWS Bedrock (gpt-*-style), GCP Vertex AI, Azure OpenAI
- Measurement: p50/p95/p99 latency per region, token throughput, cost-per-1k tokens (raw estimate), and relative caching benefits (prefix hit rate).

Notes on test variability and controls:
- Network: to reduce noise we recommend running the hyperscaler targets from the same runner cluster where possible; otherwise we’ll capture network hop timings and mark tests as customer-driven vs Redwood-run.
- Batching/Cache: small prompts benefit heavily from batching and prefix/KV caching; we’ll run both batching-on and batching-off modes for clarity.
- Residency: for eu-west1 private flows we will not send payloads outside the region — we can run in your VPC or in our Private offering (customer-managed control plane).

Attachment: geo-test-plan.md (MD, 6KB)

I’ll prep the harness (curl + small Go harness) and share instructions. Jasmine — happy to join the sync on Tue/Wed.

— Sergio
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
sergio@redwood.com
